subject: Throughput sizing follow-up: latency, throughput & peak vs steady-state
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Chris Thomas <chris.thomas@finex.com>, Aditi Patel <aditi.patel@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 9 Aug 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Throughput sizing follow-up: latency, throughput & peak vs steady-state

Hi Chris / Aditi —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size a Dedicated/Private config that meets your SLOs:

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary workload: customer support chat + post-call summarization pipeline.
- Typical request: chat turn with streaming response, average response length ~120 tokens; summarization jobs ~800 tokens.
- Expected steady-state: ~60 QPS (chat requests) during business hours.
- Peak bursts: up to 480 QPS for short windows (5–10 minutes) related to product launches.
- Concurrency: typical user concurrency target 200–300 active connections for streaming.
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 300 ms for initial token (streaming start) and end-to-end generation <= 1.2s for chat.
- Streaming: yes — client expects token-by-token streaming for UI.

Immediate asks
1) Can you share a 24–48 hour traffic sample (per-minute QPS) and an estimate of tokens/sec per request? Attachment preferred (CSV).
2) Which percentile matters most for you (p95, p99)? You mentioned p95 but want to confirm if p99 is a must-have for SLAs.
3) Any regulatory constraints around data residency or private VPC requirement?

Next steps
- If you can attach the traffic profile, we’ll run a sizing pass and propose a Dedicated pool (GPU count, instance types, and batching profile).
- Tentative technical deep-dive next Tue — Rafael + Marissa + Neha from our side.

Attachment: placeholder — we’ll accept CSV or BigQuery export.

Cheers,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

Subject: Re: Throughput sizing follow-up: latency, throughput & peak vs steady-state

Rafael / Marissa —

Attaching a 48-hour minute-level export of traffic (see attachment) and a short notes file with tokens-per-request estimates based on our telemetry. High-level answers below:

- Steady-state chat QPS: ~55–65 QPS (avg ~60).
- Peak: 420–500 QPS for up to ~8 minutes during campaigns.
- Avg tokens per chat response: 110–140 tokens.
- Summarization jobs: 700–900 tokens, ~0.5 QPS (batch job window).
- Percentiles: p95 is our consumer-facing SLO; p99 is desirable for internal monitoring but not enforced contractually.
- Streaming: required for chat UI — need low time-to-first-token (TTFT) at p95.
- Residency: US-only covered by current compliance team; however, we may ask for EU region later.

Attachment: finex_traffic_profile.csv (48h minute-level, includes tokens_per_request column) — 37KB

Let us know if you need a longer slice.

Thanks,
Chris Thomas

chris.thomas@finex.com

Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Throughput sizing follow-up: latency, throughput & peak vs steady-state

Marissa / Neha —

Forwarding FinEx traffic slice from Chris. Key asks for sizing:
- Target p95 TTFT <= 300 ms, end-to-end p95 <= 1.2s.
- Steady-state 60 QPS, bursts to 480–500 QPS for ~8–10 min.
- Streaming concurrent connections ~250.
- Tokens/request: chat 110–140, summary ~800.

Please run a quick sizing pass (back-of-envelope + recommended Dedicated config) and call out:
- GPU type and count (e.g., 8x A100s vs 16x A10G),
- Expected tokens/sec and sustained throughput,
- Recommended batching window and KV cache sizing,
- Any trade-offs to hit p95 TTFT vs cost.

Timing: FinEx asked for a proposed configuration and cost estimate by EOD Wed.

Thanks — Rafael

Chris / Aditi —

Appreciate the traffic export — that was super helpful. Quick update on next steps and what we’ll deliver:

1) Sizing pass (deliverable by EOD Wed): Rafael/Marissa/Neha will send a recommended Dedicated pool with expected token/sec, concurrency limits, and estimated monthly cost.
2) Technical deep-dive: propose Tue Aug 17 at 10am PT (Rafael + Marissa + Neha + FinEx platform + one infra SME from Redwood). Please confirm availability.
3) If the EOD Wed proposal looks good, we can schedule a 1-week proof-of-concept with telemetry to validate p95 TTFT under your peak bursts.

A few notes from our first pass:
- Based on the CSV, steady-state tokens/sec looks to be ~6k–8k total tokens/sec (chat + background jobs).
- Peak tokens/sec during bursts may reach ~65k–75k for short windows — this will drive batch sizing and buffering.
- To hit p95 TTFT <= 300ms with streaming, we’ll bias towards a lower batching window (10–20ms) and rely on KV cache for repeated prefixes. That increases GPU count for sustained peaks but improves start-of-stream latency.

Attachment: Proposed sizing will reference finex_traffic_profile.csv.

Action items for FinEx: please confirm Tue 17 10am PT or propose another slot. Also confirm p99 priority (you indicated internal monitoring only).

Regards,
